mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and suppresses earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive months of >1% INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) below their respective 12-month moving averages signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall below their 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fall below their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise above their 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon; rising housing starts signal improved residential investment and broader economic confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises month-over-month.
